persona: Same MBA student running an online concept-test survey via SurveyMonkey for a new subscription snack-box service, for a marketing research course project
source_style: raw export from SurveyMonkey (Analyze Results > Export All Responses > Excel), then lightly hand-edited without being cleaned

columns.name: Respondent ID
columns.notes: SurveyMonkey numeric respondent id, 100234501-100234538; one value (index 4) appears twice due to an accidental copy-paste duplicate row

columns.name: Collector ID
columns.notes: Constant 456789001 for every row -- single anonymous web-link collector

columns.name: Start Date
columns.notes: Datetime the response was started; all real datetimes EXCEPT one row where it was manually retyped as a text string 'MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM'

columns.name: End Date
columns.notes: Same quirk as Start Date -- one row is a text string, rest are real datetimes

columns.name: IP Address
columns.notes: Synthetic IPv4 addresses, one per respondent

columns.name: How likely are you to purchase this subscription box service?
columns.notes: 5-level text Likert: Extremely likely > Somewhat likely > Neither likely nor unlikely > Somewhat unlikely > Extremely unlikely; blank when skipped

columns.name: The price ($29.99/month) is reasonable
columns.notes: Sub-column of the matrix question in row 1 (G1:I1 merged); 5-level agreement scale; blank when skipped

columns.name: This product fits my lifestyle
columns.notes: Matrix sub-column, same agreement scale, blank when skipped

columns.name: I trust this brand
columns.notes: Matrix sub-column, same agreement scale, blank when skipped

columns.name: Amazon
columns.notes: Multi-select sub-column (K1:N1 merged group); cell = literal text 'Amazon' if selected, else blank (NOT True/False)

columns.name: Instagram Shop
columns.notes: Multi-select sub-column; cell = 'Instagram Shop' if selected, else blank

columns.name: Retailer's own website
columns.notes: Multi-select sub-column; cell = "Retailer's own website" if selected, else blank

columns.name: Other (please specify)
columns.notes: Multi-select 'Other' free-text sub-column; blank unless respondent typed a custom retailer

columns.name: Any additional comments?
columns.notes: Open-ended free text, blank for most respondents

clean_table.rule: 38 unique respondents, RespondentID = 100234501+i. Likelihood ~ weighted choice over 5 categories + skip (weights 20/25/20/15/12/8). Agreement items (PriceReasonable, FitsLifestyle, TrustBrand) each independently drawn with weights shifted toward 'agree' when Likelihood is a purchase-likely category and toward 'disagree' when unlikely, plus an 8/100 chance of being skipped (blank). AgeRange weighted toward younger brackets [30,30,20,10,7,3]. Amazon/InstagramShop/RetailerWebsite are independent Bernoulli(0.6/0.3/0.4); OtherChannel is blank ~55% of the time else one of {Etsy, TikTok Shop, Walmart.com, Costco online}. Comments filled for ~16% of respondents from a fixed pool. Seed=20260921. The physical file additionally contains: one exact duplicate of respondent #5's row (inserted at physical row 12), one fully blank row (inserted at physical row 23, a cleared disqualified respondent), and one row (physical row ~33) whose Start/End Date were manually retyped as text -- none of these three are real respondents beyond the 38 above.

intended_analysis: What share of respondents are likely/extremely likely to purchase? Is purchase likelihood associated with agreement that the price is reasonable (ordinal correlation / chi-square)? Does age range relate to which shopping channels respondents already use? Read the open-ended comments for themes.
mess_applied: Two-row header: row 1 holds question text (with two multi-column questions merged across their sub-columns, e.g. G1:I1 and K1:N1), row 2 holds the sub-question/answer-option labels for those merged groups only -- there is no single 'real header row'
Column headers are the verbatim, long question text (with punctuation, parentheses, a dollar amount) rather than short field names
Likert/agreement scales stored as text labels, not numeric codes
Multi-select checkbox question exported as one column per option, containing the option's own label text when checked and blank when not (not True/False or 1/0)
Respondent #5's entire row is duplicated verbatim elsewhere in the file (accidental copy-paste while adding notes)
One entirely blank row sitting among the data rows (a disqualified respondent whose answers were cleared but whose row was never deleted)
Start Date / End Date are real Excel datetimes for every row except one, where they were manually retyped as plain text strings
Substantial blank-cell nonresponse scattered throughout (skipped questions), not concentrated in any one column
IP Address and Collector ID columns present but analytically useless (Collector ID is constant)
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: Treating row 1 alone as the header would merge the multi-select and matrix question text into single garbled column names and lose the per-option labels in row 2; counting physical rows as 38 respondents would overstate n by including the duplicate and blank rows; treating the mixed date column as uniformly typed would error or silently coerce the one text date to null; treating blank multi-select cells as False and a filled cell as True would work, but assuming they're boolean 1/0 rather than reading the literal label would misparse them.
